The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. to role ›</a></p></div></div><h2>About the role</h2><div><p>We’re looking for a process engineer with 5+ years of experience in scaling catalytic technologies to pilot and beyond. You will play a central role in designing, constructing, and commissioning our pilot unit and subsequently designing our first commercial unit. </p>
<p><strong>Required core competencies</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>Procuring, integrating, operating, and fixing pilot-scale equipment; </li>
<li>Pilot chemical plant commissioning and operation;</li>
<li>Experience with recycling loops;</li>
<li>Experience with gas-to-liquids processes (syngas-to-methanol preferred);</li>
<li>Collaboration with EPCs in overseeing FOAK commercial unit design;</li>
<li>Experience with Aspen or other process simulation software.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Preferred qualifications</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>PLC/SCADA design and integration;</li>
<li>Experience working with modular systems; </li>
<li>Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment.</li>
</ul>
<p>As Rise Reforming scales, this role is expected to grow into a VP of Engineering or Chief Engineer position, leading a team of process and project engineers across multiple commercial deployments. <em>Senior Chemical Process Engineer</em> will report to the CTO.</p>
<p><strong>Compensation:</strong> $125,000+/year + stock options + performance bonus + benefits (health insurance, 401k).</p>
<p><strong>Location:</strong> In person, Chicago, IL and Wheaton, IL.</p>
<p>Must have a car.</p>
</div><h2>About <!-- -->Rise Reforming</h2><div><p>Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.</p>
<p>Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals like dimethyl ether (DME) and methanol. We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas. Join us!</p>
